# Summary

In assessing compliance with our [Data and Code Availability Policy](https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/journals/jpe/datapolicy), our reproducibility team has identified the following issues, which we ask you to address:

1.  You are required to cite all data also in the paper, not only the package readme.
2.  Please add the content of `codebook.csv` to the readme - this document should be the unique source of all relevant documentation, instead of having this scattered over multiple files.
3.  The description of your computational environment both local and slurm needs more detail in the readme. Locally I'm guessing you used a Mac. You need to specify exact model with specs and OS version. For the cluster versions, you need to precisely document the _exact_ hardware config you asked for on the cluster when producing your results. I need to have your slurm submit scripts as part of the package, where those configs will be clearly visible. Please say exactly how many processes/cores you used, how much RAM each, and all other relevant detail.
4.  Related to your usage of MacOS, we had a very hard time recreating your environment on Linux. This is of course not your fault, but I would ask you to look at our report and incorporate as many hints for future linux users as possible. We need a whole slew of system support libraries for this to work. It _did_ work in the end.
5.  Your readme is overall in very good shape, just needs a bit more detail.
6.  All exhibits we could feasibly reproduce are fine. I need you to add a table to your readme that shows what we were able to reproduce and what not, and the reason being "computational constraints for the JPE Data Editor". Ideally put that up front somewhere. I only need an updated version of your readme in your resubmission, leave everything else as is in the package.

# Replication

Created a Gurobi academic account, downloaded the license, and uploaded it to the working environment.

Set the Gurobi license path in the shell:

``` bash
export GRB_LICENSE_FILE=/files/gurobi.lic
```

## Initial Environment Setup

Attempted to source the setup script in local mode:

``` bash
source ./setup_env.sh local
```
This could not locate the python executable in the `.venv`. Tried fixing the virtual environment by removing `.venv`, making the setup script executable, and rerunning setup:

``` bash
rm -rf .venv
chmod +x ./setup_env.sh
./setup_env.sh local
```

-   Followed instructions as per README for linux users.
-   After this `setup_env.sh` ran to completion.
-   The full pipeline was not run due computational limitations. A shorter run based on the README was run, it only re-created the tables.

``` bash
./run.sh --steps postprocess-only --backend local
```
-   `pandas` was not found by the script. Ran:
```bash
/opt/conda/envs/amazon-carbon/bin/python -m pip install pandas
```
-   After that, it ran to completion.

## Reason for incomplete reproducibility

-   [ ] None.
-   [ ] `Discrepancy in output` (either figures or numbers in tables or text differ)
-   [ ] `Bugs in code` that were fixable by the replicator (but should be fixed in the final deposit)
-   [ ] `Code missing`, in particular if it prevented the replicator from completing the reproducibility check
    -   [ ] `Data preparation code missing` should be checked if the code missing seems to be data preparation code
-   [ ] `Code not functional` is more severe than a simple bug: it prevented the replicator from completing the reproducibility check
-   [ ] `Software not available to replicator` may happen for a variety of reasons, but in particular (a) when the software is commercial, and the replicator does not have access to a licensed copy, or (b) the software is open-source, but a specific version required to conduct the reproducibility check is not available.
-   [x] `Insufficient time available to replicator` is applicable when (a) running the code would take weeks or more (b) running the code might take less time if sufficient compute resources were to be brought to bear, but no such resources can be accessed in a timely fashion (c) the replication package is very complex, and following all (manual and scripted) steps would take too long.
-   [ ] `Data missing` is marked when data *should* be available, but was erroneously not provided, or is not accessible via the procedures described in the replication package
-   [ ] `Data not available` is marked when data requires additional access steps, for instance purchase or application procedure.
-   [ ] `Missing README` is marked if there is no README to guide the replicator, or the README is not in compliance with JPE requirements
